name: Synthesis Tutor
line: Synthesis Tutor makes K–5 math playful; AMP runs to precalculus, with a stated mastery rule and scheduled review.
description: AMP vs Synthesis Tutor: a playful K–5 app with a spoken tutor, beside AMP's path to precalculus, published mastery rule and scheduled review.
verdict: Synthesis Tutor is a highly rated app for children 5 to 11, with a spoken tutor, on-screen manipulatives and read-aloud for pre-readers [1][6][9]. It is built for kindergarten through grade 5, states no mastery threshold, and we found no scheduled review on its pages [1][2]. AMP runs from counting through precalculus, picks every problem from the learner's answers, and brings each learned skill back on a fixed schedule.

reasons.title: It keeps going after grade 5
reasons.body: Synthesis Tutor is designed for ages 5 to 11 and covers the standard K–5 curriculum [1]. Its listed topics run from counting and cardinality to fractions and algebraic thinking [1]. AMP runs from counting through precalculus in one program, 336 skills on one map. A learner who races ahead, or finishes grade 5, keeps the same record and keeps going.

reasons.title: Learned skills come back on a schedule
reasons.body: AMP brings each learned skill back after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics, and a miss restarts the schedule. We found no scheduled review of earlier lessons on Synthesis's pages [1][2][3]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' test a month later, against 38% for the same problems practiced in blocks [14].

reasons.title: A mastery rule you can read
reasons.body: Synthesis says a child moves on once they show they have understood and mastered the material, and gives no threshold [1]. In AMP a skill is Strong when four of the last five answers are right without help. An answer given after a hint or the lesson is recorded but does not count. Two misses in a row send practice to what the skill builds on.

reasons.title: Every problem chosen from the learner's answers
reasons.body: Synthesis Tutor adapts inside a lesson and moves on by lessons. On its Starter plan the child chooses lessons from a map; placement checks and a lesson planner come with Pro [1]. AMP does this for every learner: it finds the level in each of 14 strands within the first 24 problems, then picks each next problem as new work, a prerequisite, or review.

reasons.title: The method on the page, every time
reasons.body: Synthesis starts each topic with hands-on action on screen and moves to symbols after [6]. Its page for schools promises step-by-step guidance when students make mistakes [3]. AMP gives every problem type a written lesson with a worked example, and after every answer shows the correct answer and the worked steps. Each of its 961 reference lessons includes a guide for the parent. Across 55 studies, worked examples improved math performance by g = 0.48 [15].

reasons.title: Paper when the screen goes off
reasons.body: We found no workbooks or printables on Synthesis's pages, and it recommends an internet connection of 50 Mbps or faster [1][2][3]. AMP makes unlimited printable workbooks for each learner, each with a worked answer key. Results entered from paper count toward the learner's level.

rows.price: Starter $119 a year for up to seven children; Pro $239 a year; Live, with six tutor sessions, $480 a month [1][2]. Fees not refunded except where law requires [4].
rows.buyers: Families online, with a 7-day free trial and no card [1]. Schools through a sales contact, with no price published [3]. Classrooms also get it as Dojo Math in ClassDojo [8].
rows.range: Ages 5 to 11: the standard K–5 curriculum, from counting to fractions and algebraic thinking [1].
rows.start: Placement checks on the Pro plan. On Starter, the child picks lessons from a map [1].
rows.teaching: Lessons of 5 to 6 minutes, guided by a tutor with a voice and built on on-screen manipulatives [1][6][7]. Read aloud automatically for children under 7 [1].
rows.next: On Pro, a lesson planner picks the next lesson; on Starter, the child chooses. Inside a lesson, the software adapts to answers [1].
rows.mastery: The child moves on after showing understanding. No threshold is published [1].
rows.review: No scheduled review of earlier lessons found in its published materials [1][2][3].
rows.print: No workbooks or printables found in its published materials [1][2][3]. Online only, with 50 Mbps internet recommended [2].
rows.adult: Little. The maker calls it hands-off for parents and teachers. Adults set up accounts and read reports [1].
rows.reports: Progress reports. Pro adds session summaries and weekly progress emails [1]. No gradebook found in its materials for schools [3].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in the What Works Clearinghouse [5][12][13].

theirs: Synthesis Tutor is made by Synthesis, a California company founded in 2020 by Josh Dahn and Chrisman Frank. It grew out of a class at an experimental school started on the SpaceX campus in 2014 [2]. The tutor is for ages 5 to 11 and covers kindergarten through grade 5 math [1]. It runs on iPad, Android tablets and in a browser, and its App Store listing shows 4.6 stars from about 10,000 ratings [2][9]. Classrooms meet a version of it as Dojo Math inside ClassDojo [8].

A lesson runs 5 to 6 minutes and teaches one idea [7]. A tutor with a voice offers guidance on every problem [1] while the child acts on the screen: smashing a square with a hammer to see fractions, or firing a blaster to build multiplication [6]. Short checks inside each lesson decide when the child moves on [1]. Adaptive flashcards and games sit beside the lessons [9]. For children under 7, every word and answer choice is read aloud [1].

The maker's FAQ says Synthesis Tutor is not ChatGPT [1]. Its children's privacy policy gives, as examples of its AI language services, help pronouncing a child's first name and choosing grammatical gender when a lesson is translated to Spanish [8]. This page compares it as a lesson program, not a chatbot.
credit: Made for young children. Everything is read aloud for children under 7, the voice speed adjusts, and children can answer by speaking, in beta [1][9]. AMP has no read-aloud of problems.
Each topic starts with hands-on action on screen before symbols [6]. AMP has ten built-model problem types, not a manipulative at the heart of every lesson.
A lower price, most of all for big families: $119 a year covers up to seven children [2], after a 7-day trial with no card [1].
Apps for iPad and Android tablets, lessons in Spanish, games, and flashcards that track speed as well as accuracy [1][9][10]. AMP has none of these.
A human tutor when wanted: the Live plan, at $480 a month, includes six live sessions with a human tutor [1]. AMP has no live tutors.

theirs: We found no outcome study of Synthesis Tutor on its own site. Synthesis Tutor has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse (checked November 2026) [12][13].

Synthesis's blog post on whether Synthesis Tutor gets results reports no data from Synthesis Tutor [5]. It describes the DARPA Digital Tutor and says Synthesis partnered with the team that built it [5]. A 2020 summary that Synthesis links describes that program as a tutor built around 2009 to train new Navy recruits as IT workers [11]. The summary gives no number of students in each group and does not say how they were assigned [11]. It was a different product, for adults, in a different subject.

The page for schools calls the product "the world's first superhuman math tutor" and states that 98% of teachers reported improved math skills, with no source, sample or date given [3]. The pattern is the simplest one: no outcome study we could find.
ours: We built AMP's rules on findings that have held up in trials. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for blocked practice [14]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged an effect of 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [16]. AMP applies both at every problem. We expect that to show in outcomes; that is our bet, and we have committed to testing it in public.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each is registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: Your child is 5 to 8, or not yet reading, and needs every problem read aloud.
You want lessons in Spanish, or an app on an iPad or Android tablet.
You have several young children and a tight budget. One $119 plan covers up to seven.
You want math games and flashcards that track speed, or an occasional live tutor from the same company.
amp: Your child is ahead, or in grade 4 or 5, and will need math past grade 5.
You want a stated mastery rule that help cannot satisfy, and old skills brought back on a schedule.
You want to see the method: a worked example for every problem type and worked steps after every answer.
You want paper too: workbooks made for your child, with answer keys, whose results count.
You teach children of different ages and want one program from counting to precalculus.

questions.question: Is Synthesis Tutor an AI chatbot?
questions.answer: Its maker says it is not ChatGPT [1]. Its children's privacy policy gives help pronouncing a child's first name and choosing grammatical gender in Spanish translations as examples of its AI language services [8]. AMP runs no AI model while a learner works; every problem, hint and explanation comes from tested code.

questions.question: Does Synthesis Tutor cost less than AMP?
questions.answer: Yes. Starter costs $119 a year and Pro $239 a year [1]. The About page gives $29 a month or $119 a year, with one plan covering up to seven children [2]. AMP costs $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child, then $399 or $39 for each more, and covers counting through precalculus, a level in every strand, scheduled review and unlimited printable workbooks.

questions.question: Is Synthesis Tutor based on DARPA research?
questions.answer: Synthesis says it partnered with the team behind the DARPA Digital Tutor [5], which a summary Synthesis links describes as training new Navy recruits as IT workers [11]. We found no study of Synthesis Tutor itself on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in the What Works Clearinghouse [12][13].

questions.question: What should my child use after grade 5?
questions.answer: Synthesis Tutor is designed for ages 5 to 11 [1]. AMP continues through Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 and Precalculus, with the same record of every skill.

questions.question: Can we use Synthesis Tutor and AMP together?
questions.answer: Yes. They do different jobs: Synthesis Tutor introduces K–5 ideas with on-screen action [6], and AMP finds the level, schedules review and prints workbooks. AMP's first 100 answers are free, with no card.
